title: Coarse graining with sphere parameters and sizefactor > 1
purpose: Exercises the coarse-graining option of the `epsr` engine of EPSR [@soper1996,@soper2005], on when the first value of `qinscalefc` is > 1: per-molecule size factors `scalefacmol` (`.ato` molecule headers) and per-type sphere parameters `natomsph radminsph radmaxsph cgmolfac` define form factors and scale the reference-potential distances of molecule pairs [@epsrmanual]. This case sets non-default sphere parameters for every atom type and combines coarse graining with a declining box `sizefactor`.
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. Coarse graining represents atoms by uniform spheres (form factors from `gaussianqr2` of the inner and outer radius); a molecule pair scales the reference-potential distance by `scalefac = 0.5*(scalefacmol(i)+scalefacmol(j))`. Here DMSO `scalefacmol` runs from 1.00 to 1.40 in steps of 0.05 (water 1.0); the type columns are S `-0.08 0.3 1.9 2.0` (negative `natomsph` = a density, converted with `cgmolfac`), C `1.0 0.5 2.0 2.0`, O `1.0 0.0 1.5 2.0`, H `1.0 0.0 0.0 2.0`, O1 `-0.05 0.0 1.7 1.0`, H1 `1.0 0.2 0.6 0.5` (`cgmolfac` < 1 is reset to 1 on reading).
inputs: Generated from EPSR-test by `scripts/make_cg.py <folder> <mode>` (edits `.EPSR.inp` keywords, the `.ato` `scalefacmol` words and type columns). Mode for this case: `.EPSR.inp` `qinscalefc 3.0 0.5`, `ntimes 3`, `sizefactor 1.2 0.9 1.0E+06`; `.ato` as above; `.pcof` with the `rminex` values of EPSR-test-ex1.
verification: The huge threshold makes the size factor decline every iteration, 1.2 -> 1.08 -> 1.0 (clamped), which also stops intramolecular rotations while it is > 1. The three form-factor files are compared byte for byte with the standard outputs.
notes: Single-precision quirk reproduced: int((1.4-1.0)/0.2)+1 gives 2 (not 3) bins for the DMSO types. Fortran: form factors and `wavinter` are computed but never used for S(Q) (the coarse-graining code in `gensq` is commented out).
